name: Silhouette Try-On
need: See roughly how a top or dress might sit on you before you buy it — free, no account, no app.
description: A pose-guided, deliberately non-photorealistic fit preview. You supply a photo of yourself and a photo of a garment (a screenshot from a shop works well); MediaPipe's pose-landmark model finds your shoulders and hips entirely in your browser, the garment's background is lifted off with a plain classical color-distance technique, and the garment shape is warped onto your pose with a piecewise-affine mesh warp — rendered as an honestly-labeled semi-transparent overlay, not a seamless photo composite. This exists because true photorealistic try-on needs GPU-hosted generative models that cost real money per use, which is why every 'free' version on the market today rate-limits you after a few tries. This one doesn't, because nothing here costs anything to run: no photo you use is ever uploaded anywhere, and the pose-detection model (an ~18MB one-time download) runs fully offline after the page first loads.
limitations: Not photorealistic. It cannot simulate fabric, drape, stretch, or how a material actually moves — it's a warped 2D shape, honestly labeled as a preview, not a photo.
Tops and dresses only. Trousers, jackets, and structured outerwear aren't modeled by this version.

Needs a clear, front-facing, reasonably well-lit photo with your torso visible. If more than one person is in frame, it uses whichever person looks largest/closest to the camera, which may not be you. An asymmetric pose (weight on one hip, an arm raised) can visibly skew the overlay — that's an honest sketch of what was detected, not a bug.

Garment background removal is a plain-background heuristic that samples the photo's four corners — busy or textured backgrounds may not cut out cleanly. The width/length sliders exist partly to compensate.
Only shoulder/hip landmarks drive the warp; it doesn't account for arm position, so garments with distinctive sleeves may look off.

Pose detection runs synchronously on the main thread — the page can visibly pause for a few seconds while it works, worse on slower phones. The status text says so before it happens; this is a known rough edge, not a hang.

First use downloads a ~18MB pose-detection model (vendored, not from a CDN) — slow on a poor connection, but one-time and cached by the browser after. That caching is best-effort: staying on the page after going offline is verified to work, but reloading the page after going offline isn't guaranteed to.

The vendored pose-detection library (MediaPipe Tasks Vision) contains an internal call to a Google telemetry endpoint that isn't user-disableable at the library level; this app enforces a strict same-origin Content-Security-Policy so the browser itself blocks it rather than relying on removing the code. See vendor/mediapipe/NOTICE.md.
Not affiliated with any brand, retailer, or Google/MediaPipe.
evidence: https://www.mumsnet.com/talk/style_and_beauty/3974582-any-tips-on-buying-clothes-online-I-like-to-try-on-in-shops — recurring thread on fit/style uncertainty driving online-clothing returns, not damage or defects.

https://techcrunch.com/2025/12/11/googles-ai-try-on-feature-for-clothes-now-works-with-just-a-selfie/ — Google's try-on push into Search/Shopping via a metered, server-side Gemini image model, not a free client-side one.

https://genlook.app/blog/google-doppl-shuts-down-migration — Google shut down its standalone Doppl try-on app in April 2026, folding the feature into that metered server-side model — independent confirmation from the best-resourced player that zero-cost client-side photoreal try-on isn't a solved problem yet.

https://magichour.ai/products/virtual-try-on — a 'free' competitor that rate-limits to 3 generations/day then paywalls, because each generation costs real inference money; the gap a zero-marginal-cost client-side tool fills.

https://www.stytrix.com/blog/best-free-ai-virtual-try-on-tools-2026-comparison — 2026 roundup of 'free' try-on tools, all metered/paywalled after a handful of uses, corroborating the pattern above across multiple products rather than one.
